title: Distributed Logging & Search
summary: Ingest distributed logs into searchable hot indices and durable cold archives while streaming live matches.
narrative:
Agents on every EC2 host tail files, retain their read positions and batch log lines. The Client represents both these host agents and the engineer's browser for search and live tail. Plan for ~1 M lines/s: at ~120 bytes per line that is ~120 MB/s, or ~10 TB/day of raw logs, which compresses to roughly ~1 TB/day (~10:1) in the archive. Engineers need full-text search over the last 7 days in seconds and a 1-year cold archive in object storage.

Route ingestion and query traffic through a Load Balancer to Web Servers. Ingestion appends to replicated Message Queues, which buffer bursts before a Stream Processor parses, enriches and indexes records. Store the hot tier in time-partitioned Search Index shards with replicas, and write compressed raw batches to Blob Storage for cold retention and reindexing. The Web Server query path selects relevant time indices, searches shards and merges results; archival retrieval requires reading or reindexing cold objects rather than pretending they are a live full-text index.

For live tail, publish processed lines through Pub/Sub to a WebSocket Server reached through the Load Balancer. The WebSocket tier checks the browser's authorized subscriptions and streams new matching lines, with bounded buffering and reconnect handling. Replicate Web Servers, queue brokers and search nodes; optionally cache recent query results and add Monitoring for ingestion lag and index failures. Assemble this service from ingestion, buffering, processing and storage components: it is itself the log aggregator.

functional: Collect batched log lines from host agents through the ingestion API
Queue, parse, enrich and index logs in the Search Index
Retain 7 searchable days and archive raw logs in Blob Storage for 1 year
Query relevant time-partitioned indices and return merged full-text results
Publish new lines through Pub/Sub and stream authorized matches over WebSockets
nonFunctional: Sustain ~1 M lines/s with buffering and backpressure for bursts
Search the last 7 days in seconds
Maintain ingestion and hot search through a single web-server, broker or search-node failure
constraints: Clients must query the Search Index through the Web Server API
Web Server ingestion reaches Stream Processors through the Message Queue
Build the aggregation service from its parts rather than using the Log Aggregator component
Separate raw-object retention from searchable hot indices and enforce subscription access controls
capacity: ~1 M lines/s × ~120 B/line ≈ 120 MB/s ≈ 10 TB/day raw; ≈ 1 TB/day after ~10:1 compression
Hot tier: ~70 TB of raw logs for 7 days before index overhead and replicas; cold archive: ~365 TB/year compressed
specs.tradeoff: Time-partitioned hot indices make recent search fast but consume more space than compressed raw objects. Cold storage reduces retention cost while requiring slower retrieval or reindexing. Live tail provides immediate matches but needs bounded per-client buffering so a slow browser cannot stall ingestion.
specs.bonus: Connect Web Server → Cache for recent query results and add Monitoring for backlog, processing errors and search health.

topologyRules.message: Clients search through the Web Server API instead of accessing indices directly.
Log ingestion must pass through the Message Queue before parsing and indexing.

resilienceRules.message: Run at least two Web Servers for ingestion and search availability.
Run at least two Message Queue brokers with replicated ingestion buffers.
Run at least two Search Index nodes with replicated shards for hot-search availability.

hints: Start with Client → Load Balancer → Web Server → Message Queue. The Client covers host agents as well as browsers; buffer ingestion before parsing.

Connect Message Queue → Stream Processor → Search Index and → Blob Storage for hot search and cold archive. Add Web Server → Search Index for queries, then Stream Processor → Pub/Sub → WebSocket Server and Load Balancer → WebSocket Server for live tail.

Use two Web Servers, two Message Queues and two Search Index nodes. Connect each Web Server to both brokers and both search nodes; both brokers feed the processor, which indexes into both search nodes. Preserve the archive and live-tail paths, then add each Web Server → Cache and → Monitoring.
